summary: Situated 3D reasoning requires embodied agents to interpret objects, scene geometry, and viewpoint dependent spatial relations. Existing methods learn grounded interactions from supervised traces, but largely imitate prescribed evidence acquisition patterns rather than optimizing the support that the returned evidence provides for the correct answer.
takeaways: To this end, this paper presents CARE-3D, a reinforcement post-training framework for adaptive grounded reasoning.
An effective agent should instead adaptively decide what to ground, which tool to invoke, and how to assess the utility of returned evidence.

Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on grounding instructions first establishes valid interactions, after which Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) optimizes the agent while keeping the 3D grounding module frozen.
